task.description: Implement REQ-027 per lib/letflow/design/req027-definition-core-schema.md, which passed the Step 1b hard gate unmodified (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS, handoff b6fa30b, ~40 citations re-derived with zero fabrications). Build two migrations and two Ecto.Schema modules, apply the mandatory prefix() guard to both migrations, and append manifest entries eight and nine while preserving all seven existing ones. Three carry-forward corrections from the design gate are listed in the dispatch prompt and must not be dropped. Demonstrate acceptance criteria 1-4 with real quoted output against a genuinely provisioned tenant schema -- in particular the two PARTIAL index predicates and the FK's absent ON DELETE action, which are silent-correctness properties that a passing compile would not reveal.
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains process_definitions and instance_definition_snapshots migrations, both schema-per-tenant via REQ-022's :prefix mechanism, applying cleanly
process_definitions has a unique index on (name, version) and a partial unique index on name WHERE status = 'active'
process_definitions has a nullable stage column and a partial index on stage WHERE stage IS NOT NULL, per definition.md's PD-07 section (migrations/014_definition_stage.sql)
instance_definition_snapshots.definition_id references process_definitions.id with no ON DELETE CASCADE, and the moduledoc states this is deliberate per PD-08
both Ecto.Schema modules' @moduledoc cite R-Co src/design/definition.md (PD-01/PD-07/PD-08 sections) as the ported source
mix compile --warnings-as-errors exits 0 and mix format --check-formatted exits 0
the existing suite does not regress (baseline 271 passing) and both shipped policing tests still pass with the manifest at nine entries

result.summary: REQ-027 implemented exactly as lib/letflow/design/req027-definition-core-schema.md (commit a15bce4) specifies -- two migrations, two Ecto.Schema modules, and the two-entry manifest append. No divergence from the gate-approved design. IMPLEMENTED: (1) priv/repo/migrations/20260816193001_create_process_definitions.exs and (2) .../20260816193002_create_instance_definition_snapshots.exs, both with REQ-022 §4's mandatory `if prefix() do ... end` guard and a no-op nil branch, modelled on the shipped 20260816120003_create_instance_projections.exs. (3) lib/letflow/definitions/process_definition.ex and (4) lib/letflow/definitions/instance_definition_snapshot.ex. (5) lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex: manifest entries eight and nine appended in the three-element {version, module, filename} form, all seven existing entries preserved byte-for-byte, and `tenant_scoped_migrations/0`'s @spec confirmed byte-identical (`git diff -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex | grep '@spec'` returns nothing). Both 'seven entries' prose sites in the @doc/header comment updated to nine. || COMPILE: `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> 'Compiling 3 files (.ex) / Generated letflow app', EXIT=0. FORMAT: `mix format --check-formatted` -> EXIT=0 (no output). || CATALOG PROOF (AC 1-4), taken from the LIVE Postgres catalog against a genuinely provisioned non-default tenant schema, not from migration source. Method: insert Tenant -> TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 -> replay_migrations/2 -> query pg_indexes / pg_index / pg_constraint / information_schema -> DROP SCHEMA CASCADE. Probe schema: tenant_c080899740524c49bea4025ee525f69d, database letflow_test2 (asserted in-script; the script refuses to run against any other database). replay_migrations/2 applied 9 versions: [20260816120001, 20260816120002, 20260816120003, 20260816120004, 20260816120005, 20260816120006, 20260816163103, 20260816193001, 20260816193002]; tenant_scoped_migrations/0 length = 9. || AC 1 -- 'SELECT table_schema, table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_name IN (...)' across the whole database returned ONLY: 'tenant_c080899740524c49bea4025ee525f69d.instance_definition_snapshots' and 'tenant_c080899740524c49bea4025ee525f69d.process_definitions'. Per-table: 'process_definitions: in tenant_c0808997...? true | in public? false'; 'instance_definition_snapshots: in tenant_c0808997...? true | in public? false'. NEGATIVE PROOF OF THE GUARD, independently re-checked via psql after a plain prefix-less `mix ecto.migrate` had already run and recorded both versions in public.schema_migrations: `SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name IN ('process_definitions','instance_definition_snapshots')` -> 0. || AC 2 -- verbatim indexdef from pg_indexes: 'CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_definition_version ON tenant_c0808997....process_definitions USING btree (name, version)' and 'CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_active_definition ON tenant_c0808997....process_definitions USING btree (name) WHERE ((status)::text = 'active'::text)'. Corroborated from pg_index: 'uq_definition_version unique=true partial=false predicate=nil'; 'uq_active_definition unique=true partial=true predicate="((status)::text = 'active'::text)"'. || AC 3 -- 'CREATE INDEX idx_def_stage ON tenant_c0808997....process_definitions USING btree (stage) WHERE (stage IS NOT NULL)'; pg_index: 'idx_def_stage unique=false partial=true predicate="(stage IS NOT NULL)"'. information_schema.columns: 'stage character varying nullable=YES default=nil'. || AC 4 -- pg_constraint on instance_definition_snapshots: 'instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey / contype="f" confdeltype="a" confupdtype="a" / FOREIGN KEY (definition_id) REFERENCES tenant_c0808997....process_definitions(id)'. confdeltype is 'a' (NO ACTION), NOT 'c' (CASCADE), and pg_get_constraintdef emits no ON DELETE clause at all. Constraint name is Ecto's default and is byte-identical to R-Co's. || SILENT-CORRECTNESS PROPERTIES, demonstrated behaviourally because both would ship green if wrong. (a) status is stored LOWERCASE and the enum dump agrees with the index predicate: raw `SELECT status` after inserting through ProcessDefinition.create_changeset/2 returned "draft"; promoting a first definition to :active succeeded, promoting a SECOND definition with the same name to :active was rejected -> {:rejected, :unique_violation, "uq_active_definition"}. That proves uq_active_definition matches real rows rather than zero rows, i.e. PD-03's single-active-per-name invariant is genuinely enforced (design INV-DEF-3). (b) The FK's NO ACTION genuinely rejects a parent delete and the snapshot survives: `Repo.delete(definition)` -> {:rejected, "instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey", :foreign_key}, and the snapshot row was still readable afterwards (true). A dangling definition_id returned {:error, changeset} with errors=[definition_id: {"does not exist", [constraint: :foreign, constraint_name: "instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey"]}] rather than raising, and snapshotted_at came back from the DB default via read_after_writes (~U[2026-08-16 20:08:52.918975Z]). Probe schema dropped: 'probe schema tenant_c0808997... still exists? false'; psql confirms zero remaining tenant_% schemas in letflow_test2. letflow_test and letflow_dev were never touched (both report 0 tables named process_definitions/instance_definition_snapshots). || TESTS: `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test --seed 0` -> 'Finished in 16.8 seconds (0.8s async, 15.9s sync) / Result: 271 passed (4 properties, 267 tests)', EXIT=0 -- exactly the 271 baseline, no regression. Re-run with a random seed -> 'Result: 271 passed (4 properties, 267 tests)'. ISS-0011's tenant_status_test.exs:121 flake did not fire in either run. The two shipped policing tests pass with the manifest at nine entries, named explicitly via --trace: '§4 guard pattern -- every registered tenant-scoped migration is a real no-op without a prefix / every migration registered in tenant_scoped_migrations/0 creates nothing in public when run with no :prefix (§4 guard pattern) (161.5ms)' and 'tenant_scoped_migrations/0 manifest consistency / each registered migration's version matches the numeric prefix of the file it was actually loaded from (2.5ms)' plus 'registered migration versions are unique and strictly ascending (1.7ms)'. migrations_test.exs alone: 'Result: 13 passed'. || TWO EXTRA INDEXES, DISCLOSED FOR REVIEWER'S STEP 2d SCOPE-CREEP CHECK. Beyond REQ-027's three enumerated indexes (uq_definition_version, uq_active_definition, idx_def_stage) this implementation creates two more, both specified by the gate-approved design §3.1.2/§3.2.1 and both sourced from R-Co rather than invented: (1) idx_def_status on process_definitions(status), non-unique, no predicate -- R-Co migrations/004_definitions.sql:39, justified because it serves REQ-030's list/1 `?status=` filter (definition.md:1447); (2) idx_snap_definition on instance_definition_snapshots(definition_id), non-unique -- R-Co 004_definitions.sql:68-69 verbatim, justified as load-bearing rather than decorative: Postgres does not automatically index the REFERENCING side of a foreign key, so without it every DELETE FROM process_definitions must sequentially scan the snapshot table to evaluate the FK's NO ACTION check -- the exact delete path REQ-033 AC 4 exercises. Both appear in the quoted pg_indexes output above. Correspondingly, the design's 'deliberately NOT created' list is honoured: idx_def_name (redundant behind uq_definition_version's leading column), idx_def_fts (not ported on PD-10's own authority -- its ILIKE query cannot use a to_tsvector GIN index), and the four 028_adp02 tenant-prefixed variants (degenerate under Decision B's schema-as-tenant-boundary). Each absence is documented with its reason in the migration header. || THE THREE CARRY-FORWARD CORRECTIONS FROM THE DESIGN GATE, ALL APPLIED. (1) PD-08 cross-reference added to ProcessDefinition's moduledoc: its 'Ported source' section now names the PD-01 and PD-07 sections AND adds 'The same document's PD-08 section is the ported source for instance_definition_snapshots, the table that references this one -- see Letflow.Definitions.InstanceDefinitionSnapshot, whose foreign key onto process_definitions.id deliberately carries no ON DELETE CASCADE.' Both moduledocs therefore now name PD-01, PD-07 and PD-08 explicitly, satisfying acceptance criterion 5 on its most literal reading. (2) The two extra indexes are disclosed in the paragraph above rather than left for REVIEWER to discover. (3) The six immaterial citation drifts were corrected where carried into code comments: connection.ex:1339 -> :1335 for `quote_name(index.prefix, index.table)` (re-verified by reading deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/postgres/connection.ex directly -- 1335 is the prefix/table render, 1344 is the `if_do(index.where, ...)` WHERE emission), and `:bigserial` renders as `bigint`, not `integer` (`reference_column_type(:bigserial, _opts), do: "bigint"` at connection.ex:1902) -- the snapshot migration's header states bigint. All other cited mechanisms were re-verified independently before use: enum.ex:81-83's `{:string, Enum.map(values, fn atom -> {atom, to_string(atom)} end)}`, migration.ex:513-514's `type: :bigserial` / `on_delete: :nothing` struct defaults, connection.ex:1918's `reference_on_delete(_), do: []`, connection.ex:1872's ref-prefix fallback, and connection.ex:1895-1896's default fkey name. || SELF-REVIEW (WF-02 Step 2a point 8): no SQL string interpolation of tenant/user input -- both migrations use the Ecto.Migration DSL exclusively, the sole fragment/1 is a constant string with no interpolation, and neither schema module contains SQL (INV-7 / design INV-DEF-10 satisfied); no bare `{:ok, _} =` match on an external-I/O path in either new module; no gen_statem, supervision tree, or state transition touched, so the one-process-per-instance model and synchronous-persistence rule are untouched and README's ASCII diagram needs no change; every new public function (ProcessDefinition.create_changeset/2, ProcessDefinition.update_changeset/2, InstanceDefinitionSnapshot.create_changeset/2) carries a @doc; no existing function signature changed. Migrations are additive and auto-reversible -- change/0 with create table / create index / create unique_index / references-inside-create-table only, no execute/1 and no raw SQL. Per the design's normative 'functions that will deliberately NOT exist' table, InstanceDefinitionSnapshot exposes no update_changeset/2, no generic changeset/2 and no delete path (write-once, INV-DEF-6); ProcessDefinition exposes no status-mutating changeset, no transition_allowed?/2 and no Repo call (REQ-030's scope). Neither module declares @schema_prefix (INV-DEF-7) or a belongs_to association.

issues.description: Incidental, pre-existing, NOT introduced by REQ-027 and NOT fixed here: priv/repo/migrations/ is outside .formatter.exs's `inputs` ("{mix,.formatter}.exs", "{config,lib,test}/**/*.{ex,exs}"), and .formatter.exs declares no `import_deps: [:ecto_sql]`. Consequence: `mix format --check-formatted` (the real gate, EXIT=0) never inspects any migration file, and running the formatter explicitly on one rewrites Ecto.Migration's locals_without_parens macros into the parenthesised form -- `add :x, :binary_id` becomes `add(:x, :binary_id)`. Verified this is pre-existing and affects the shipped tree identically: `mix format --check-formatted priv/repo/migrations/20260816120003_create_instance_projections.exs` exits 1 with exactly the same class of diff. REQ-027's two migrations follow the established unparenthesised house style of every shipped migration, so they are consistent with the tree as it stands. Not fixed here because adding `import_deps: [:ecto_sql]` plus a migrations glob would reformat all sixteen migration files -- far outside REQ-027's scope, and it should be its own change. Not filed as a new ISS-NNNN per the dispatch instruction to report incidental findings in result.issues rather than self-filing; ORCH may wish to register it.

Design OQ-2 confirmed empirically, forwarded to REQ-033 rather than reinterpreted. REQ-033's fourth acceptance criterion is worded 'deleting the source process_definitions row (where FK rules permit, e.g. a DRAFT definition) does not remove or invalidate an existing snapshot row'. Under the NO ACTION FK that REQ-027 AC 4 mandates, that parenthetical describes a case that does not exist: the catalog proof above shows the delete is REJECTED outright -- {:rejected, "instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey", :foreign_key} -- regardless of the parent's status. The behaviour is correct and satisfies PD-08 a fortiori (the snapshot survives), but a REQ-033 test written to the criterion's literal wording would fail against a correct schema. REQ-033's test must assert the delete is rejected AND the snapshot still readable. Stated in InstanceDefinitionSnapshot's moduledoc so it is discoverable from the code.

No disagreement with the design artefact. Implemented as designed, with zero silent divergence; nothing needed routing back to CODE-DESIGNER. Recorded explicitly so the absence of a disagreement is an affirmative statement rather than an omission. The design's own OQ-1 (who supplies process_definitions.tenant_id, which is NOT NULL with no DB default) and OQ-6 (no requirement owns a hard-delete path for process_definitions) remain open and are REQ-030's to resolve; both are carried forward unchanged, not resolved here.
